belgian_waffle_ride.aid_stations: 6 feed zones on the 2026 Waffle course. Comprehensive course marking.
rider_intel_notes: The course included quite a bit more rough off-road sections, which meant more people considered it a gravel race instead of a road race with off-road sectors.
belgian_waffle_ride.surface: 53% unroad and 47% pavement on the 2026 Waffle, mixing gravel, deep sand, rocks, doubletrack, decomposed granite, dirt, and singletrack across 30 unroad sectors.

rider_intel_notes: The course has a reputation for category 2 or category 3 type gravel with particularly sharp rocks that cause frequent flats.
The 50-mile course is actually a lot smoother than the 100 mile course, according to pros.
big_sugar.surface: Loose, rocky gravel on rarely maintained Ozark roads. The course includes a few pavement sections, water crossings, and bridges.

boulder_roubaix.aid_stations: Neutral support based on volunteer availability — unlikely. Self-supported. Bring pump, spare tube, and do a bolt check.
features: Unpaved county roads — ranging from smooth to extremely rutted depending on weather
Rolling terrain with no sustained major climbs but constant undulation
Mixed-surface transitions between pavement and dirt — the defining tactical element
Winding curves through North Boulder County open space and farmland
New 2026 finish along Boulder Feeder Canal and across reservoir dams
boulder_roubaix.surface: 61% unpaved, 39% paved (2026 course). The unpaved sections are real working county and farm roads — not manicured gravel. Surface quality ranges from smooth hard-pack to deeply rutted washboard depending on weather conditions leading up to race day. The 2026 course adds a challenging finish along the Boulder Feeder Canal and across the Boulder Reservoir dams.

dirty_kanza_200.aid_stations: 2 full checkpoints + 2 water oases. Everything between those points is on you, your crew, and whatever you can fix in the ditch.
dirty_kanza_200.surface: Chunky limestone that shreds tires and hands

gravel_worlds.aid_stations: Multiple aid stations at key points
rider_intel_notes: Roads are in primo shape for much of the course but there are many sections of deep gravel that require you to stay relaxed and let the bike float to avoid slipping and sliding.
The terrain is more relentless than Unbound with constant up and down roller coasters. There are no flat roads in Nebraska and the surfing motion over hills zaps your legs.
gravel_worlds.surface: Loose gravel, some rough minimum maintenance, occasional sand/mud

leadville_100.aid_stations: 8+ aid stations with crew access points
rider_intel_notes: It's more of a dirt road race done on mountain bikes rather than traditional mountain biking terrain.
leadville_100.surface: Variable: buffed singletrack to rocky jeep roads to pavement

mid_south.aid_stations: Miles ~30, 60. Water, snacks, neutral support. Sparse but sufficient.
features: Surface quality depends entirely on weather
rider_intel_notes: Red dirt roads that can be chunky in sections. If the mud gets wet, it becomes very problematic for traction and bike handling.
Surprisingly not sketchy on descents despite being DIY roads, though riders report being puckered up on the descents due to conditions.
mid_south.surface: 98-99% unpaved Oklahoma red clay (iron oxide). Hard-pack when dry = slick center tread tires work well. 'Peanut butter mud' when wet—wheels stop spinning. Not the chunky gravel of Unbound.

rider_intel_notes: The champagne gravel is described as fine little pebbles like bubbles in champagne. It's fast, so fast, making Steamboat Gravel historically a fast course.
Course becomes extremely dusty immediately after the first gravel section. Riders report being covered in dust and bikes becoming completely filthy very early in the race.
There are rocks flying everywhere. There are crashes happening. It's just a beatdown. To race 200 miles on this terrain is just so destructive.

The conditions are completely unexpected. It's so different to everything we do. There's a lot of different sections to approach. Some are famous for being really fast. Some are famous for people notoriously having punctures non-stop and some are just famous for being real tough, gritty sections.
unbound_gravel_100.surface: ~90% unpaved chunky flint rock roads, ~10% paved transfers. Sharp stones slice sidewalls. Clay mud when wet becomes 'peanut butter' that stops bikes.

unbound_gravel_200.aid_stations: 2 full checkpoints + 2 water oases. Everything between those points is on you, your crew, and whatever you can fix in the ditch.
unbound_gravel_200.surface: Chunky limestone that shreds tires and hands

rider_intel_notes: Sharp rocks are a constant hazard on the course that riders must navigate.
The course features rolling terrain that becomes more challenging as heat builds throughout the day.
unbound_xl.surface: 350 miles of sharp, chunky Flint Hills limestone that shreds tires. Rolling prairie terrain.
